messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: SEV2 for tenant 'specter' (enterprise, VPC) in us-east-1 — traffic spike + 502s; potential regional capacity issue. Pager: leo_oncall
leo_oncall: ack. I'm awake, looking at logs now. Can someone drop quick impact summary for customer-facing team? :eyes:
jamie_sre: I'm pulling metrics. Seeing ~40% of requests hitting 502/timeout on specter dedicated pool in us-east-1 since 23:12 UTC. Other regions look normal. KV-cache fill rate spiked, GPU utilization at 95% on pool nodes. Logs show repeated OOM-ish failures in inference-runtime.
morgan_runtime: @jamie_sre can you paste the pod logs? Also check warm pool standing by capacity, we may need to warm additional nodes.
jamie_sre: paste: ```[2025-11-03T23:13:02Z] ERROR runtime::alloc - failed to allocate kv-cache 1.2G on device gpu0; evicting entries
[2025-11-03T23:13:05Z] ERROR http - downstream 502 serving request /v1/generate tenant=specter trace=abc123```
jamie_sre: warm pool shows 2 warm hosts reserved for specter in us-east-1 (min_ready=2), but autoscale didn't kick — control plane shows burst_disabled flag set for that tenant (policy override).
leo_oncall: customer is in active commerce window — tara_account can you confirm SLA and whether to initiate traffic shift? Also confirm if DNS failover is allowed (customer's VPC/KMS policies may restrict).
tara_account: Confirmed. Specter has enterprise SLA and allowed migration to standby region per contract but only after we notify them and rotate keys. They prefer we try warm capacity before DNS cutover. I'll open a bridge to their oncall. nisha_support joining.
alex_netops: Quick network note: us-east-1 to us-west-2 path is healthy. If we do DNS shift, we can either update Route53 weighted routing or do a customer-side BGP shift (they run a private edge). Which is preferred?
ops_lead: For speed, we should try internal routing first: smart routing policy -> route their traffic to dedicated standby pool in us-west-2 (same dedicated tenant pools already provisioned). DNS cutover is last-resort; it's heavier and needs customer coordination.
morgan_runtime: I can initiate routing override. Precheck: are model versions compatible on west pool? We onboarded a quantized variant there last month. Need to allow fallback to compatible variant.
jamie_sre: Model variant on west is quantized-8bit-v2, compatible with requests (we have fallback mapping in runtime config). Latency there will be +30-50ms, but stable.
leo_oncall: Ok step plan:
1) Initiate temporary routing override to west (rate limit 30% -> 100% in 10m increments) and monitor errors.
2) If errors persist after 20m, escalate to DNS cutover.
3) Notify specter ops + rotate keys if we need cross-region access.
I'll start step 1 now.
leo_oncall: /incident route-override specter us-west-2 weight=30 duration=10m — command issued
incident-bot: Command accepted: route-override specter -> us-west-2 weight=30 duration=10m. Watch metrics at https://console.redwood/specter/incidents/2212346789
jamie_sre: Monitoring: errors down to 25% in first 2m, about 15% of traffic shifted. GPU utilization in us-east still high but dropping.
nisha_support: I messaged specter oncall (specter-oncall@specter.com) — letting them know we're routing traffic to standby pools and will avoid DNS change unless needed. They want regular updates every 10 minutes. :thumbsup:
tara_account: Specter replied: "Thanks — prefer we avoid DNS if possible. Please keep us posted."
leo_oncall: Increase to 60% now. /incident route-override specter us-west-2 weight=60 duration=10m
incident-bot: Command accepted: route-override specter -> us-west-2 weight=60 duration=10m.
jamie_sre: Update: error rate down to 4% overall. us-east pool still has ~10% errors on remaining traffic but degradation is minor. Latency on west is +45ms median.
ops_lead: Nice. Keep monitoring for 15 more minutes. Trigger rollback if west starts to saturate.
alex_netops: Note: route override will only affect host-level routing; DNS TTLs unchanged. If we need full-region failover (eg. for capacity), we'll coordinate DNS change later.
leo_oncall: After 18m of stability, I'll start handing off to night SRE. @jamie_sre can you prepare a short RCA draft of root cause for the oncall handoff message? Include kv-cache OOM and burst_disabled flag on control plane.
jamie_sre: Will do. Drafting now.
incident-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff in 12 minutes. Next: jamie_sre will take over monitoring. Escalation channel #eng-runtime if errors > 15%.
jamie_sre: Handoff note: root cause looks like unexpected KV-cache growth from a new prompt pattern that increased lifetime of cached keys; control-plane policy disabled burst to prevent noisy neighbor cost spikes — that prevented autoscaling. Mitigation: route-override to west and re-enable burst for specter while we patch eviction policy. I'll attach logs and config diffs.
leo_oncall: Handoff ack. Leaving the channel. leo_oncall sign-off :wave:
morgan_runtime: Re-enabled burst for specter (temporary override). /controlplane set-burst specter enable temp-30m
incident-bot: Control plane change applied: burst enabled for specter for 30m. Audit ID: cp-audit-7782
nisha_support: Customer confirmed they see degraded UX early on but now recovering. They're setting a status banner internally; no external incident page needed.
tara_account: I'm scheduling a follow-up with specter for 10:00 UTC tomorrow for a postmortem and key rotation talk.
jamie_sre: I'll keep monitoring and start the RCA doc in #postmortems/specter.
ops_lead: Closing notes: no DNS cutover required, traffic shifted via routing override, warm capacity + burst re-enable mitigated. We'll run a replay test on staging to reproduce KV-cache growth pattern.
jamie_sre: final metrics snapshot: peak 95% GPU util (us-east), errors 40% -> 4% after 60% shift, steady-state latency +45ms in west. Closing thread unless anyone needs further action.
alex_netops: Thanks team. I'll create a config ticket to ensure auto-enable of burst for enterprise tenants when pool utilization >85%.
nisha_support: Marking customer as informed. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident thread 2212346789 marked RESOLVED by leo_oncall at 23:55 UTC. Postmortem scheduled.
